rows.text: 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ entities (Avogadro constant, Nₐ). Molar mass (M) is g·mol⁻¹; for a compound M = Σ(atomic masses).  ·  n (mol) = mass/M = volume(ideal gas, STP)/22.4 L = N/Nₐ.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **The mole.** One mole contains 6.022 × 10²³ entities (Avogadro's number, Nₐ); the molar mass M in g/mol equals the atomic or molecular mass numerically.  ·  **Mass–moles conversion.** n = m/M; for example 36 g of water (M = 18 g/mol) is 2 mol. One mole of any gas at STP occupies 22.4 L.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Percentage composition.** The percentage of an element = (mass of the element in one mole of compound ÷ molar mass) × 100.  ·  **Empirical and molecular formula.** The empirical formula gives the simplest atomic ratio and the molecular formula the actual count; molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass gives the multiplier.  ·  **Limiting reagent and yield.** The limiting reagent governs product mass; percentage yield = (actual yield ÷ theoretical yield) × 100.
